paraphrase: The setting: the Bhagavat, the great enjoyment body, whose nature is the vajra body, speech and mind of all the tathāgatas of the ten directions and four times, abides in Akaniṣṭha in a boundless palace of blazing wisdom-jewels; around him are the tathāgatas named the king of consciousness, the king of form, the king of feeling, the king of perception and so on — the aggregates themselves as the buddhas.
speaker: the tantra's narrator

location.section: D832 ff. 124a.1-124b.3 (chapter 13, shin tu gsang ba man ngag gi le'u)

paraphrase: The most secret instruction: the maṇḍala of Samantabhadra, gazed upon by the five wisdoms, is spontaneously perfect; this is the great secret fruit taken as the path, by which the five kāyas are spontaneously perfected — there is no more secret definitive meaning in all the victors' maṇḍalas. It is to be given only to those with the eye of wisdom trained in hearing, reflection and meditation, fit vessels of good character who offer body and wealth — never otherwise; if it is proclaimed to the deluded, their life ends untimely and they remain long burning and scorched.
notes: Passage located and read in the local Derge e-text (folio in location.section); paraphrase by U45 from the Tibetan (skeleton phase, fidelity not yet checked). Chapter 13 is the chapter on which the Garland of Views (src:mengak-tawai-trengwa) comments.

paraphrase: The generation of the primordially enlightened mind as wisdom: 'E ma'o! This wondrous, marvellous dharma, the secret of all perfect buddhas: from the unborn all is born, and in being born there is no birth.' The same is said of ceasing, abiding, objects of observation, and coming and going: from what does not cease, abide, observe or come and go, everything ceases, abides, is observed, comes and goes — and in doing so does not.
speaker: the great being of non-duality (gnyis su med pa'i bdag nyid chen po)

paraphrase: Out of great compassion, since beings, though of one nature with the buddhas, wander through the five classes by the conceptuality of ignorance: 'E ma! From the sugata-essence, by one's own conceptual karma are emanated bodies, enjoyments, abodes, sufferings and the rest, and one grasps them as I and mine. No one binds; there is no bondage and nothing to be bound. Grasping a self through conceptuality, one forcibly ties knots in space. The buddha-dharma, spontaneously perfect from the beginning, without bondage or liberation, displays varied activity in order to be taught.'

location.section: D832 f. 113a.1-7 (chapter 3, chos thams cad gtan la phab pa)

paraphrase: The six sages emanated from the buddhas' body, speech and mind teach, according to those to be tamed, the vehicles of gods and humans, of śrāvakas, of pratyekabuddhas, of bodhisattvas and the unsurpassed vehicle: eighty-four thousand teachings as antidotes to the eighty-four thousand afflictions arising from ignorant conceptuality. All of them show that grasped and grasper arise interdependently, that karma and its result are not wasted, and ultimately that one is not stained by karma and its result.

paraphrase: The wheel of the garland of syllables: without moving from the samādhi in which all phenomena are primordially enlightened, the tathāgatas bring forth the syllables in which all phenomena abide as mere names. From the stable white A, extremely subtle A's radiate, filling the ten directions, and are gathered without increase or decrease; from them all groups of names blaze forth and are gathered — the cause of the stable wisdom of vajra accomplishment. The alphabet is uttered, the six worlds quake, and all phenomena become mere marks of names. 'A is neither empty nor not empty, and no middle is found either; all buddhas, mere names, abide in the garland of syllables; A itself appears as the variety, ka and the rest.'
notes: Passage located and read in the local Derge e-text (folio in location.section); paraphrase by U45 from the Tibetan (skeleton phase, fidelity not yet checked). The link to the Dzogchen 'sound, light and rays' concept is thematic (sound as display), added by the unit.
